title: A linear upper bound on the $\mathbb{Z}_p$-Ramsey number of graphs with sufficiently large $2$-packing
summary: Given a positive integer $k$ and graph $G$, the $\mathbb{Z}_k$-Ramsey number $R(G,\mathbb{Z}_k)$ is the least $N$ (if it exists) such that every coloring $f:E(K_N)\rightarrow \mathbb{Z}_k$ contains a copy $G'$ of $G$ such that $\sum_{e\in E(G')}f(e)=0$. Motivated by a question of Caro and Mifsud, we study the $\mathbb{Z}_k$-Ramsey number of graphs with a sufficiently large 2-packing, i.e. a set of vertices $S\subseteq V(G)$ such that $N[u]\cap N[v]=\emptyset$ for all distinct $u,v\in S$.
